statement: Given a dataset of observed data points and a model instantiated by estimated model parameters, the consensus set (the set of confirmed inliers) is the subset of data points from the dataset that fit the model within a specified error threshold: $S_{\text{consensus}} = \{ x \in \text{data} \mid \text{error}(x, \text{model}) < t \}$.

symbols.meaning: consensus set (set of inliers confirmed for the instantiated model)
input set of observed data points containing inliers and outliers
mathematical model instantiated with parameters estimated from a minimal sample subset
error threshold value defining the maximum data deviation for inliers
threshold number of inliers required to assert that the model fits well to the data

properties.property: In the original RANSAC formulation, candidate models are evaluated and ranked by the cardinality of their consensus set.
properties.why: Higher cardinality indicates that more data features consistently agree on the model.

properties.property: If the consensus set cardinality exceeds threshold $d$, the model parameters are re-estimated using all members of the consensus set.
properties.why: Re-estimating over all confirmed inliers refines and sharpens model fitting quality compared to estimating from only the minimal sample subset.

properties.property: In M-estimator variants (MSAC and MLESAC), consensus set quality is evaluated using likelihood rather than simple cardinality.
properties.why: Likelihood evaluation mitigates the drawback of treating all data points within the error threshold equally.

assumptions.assumption: Data elements consist of inliers that fit the model parameters subject to noise, and outliers that do not fit the model.
assumptions.breaks_when: Noise is indistinguishable from outlier deviations, or non-inlier points fit the model due to ambiguity.

assumptions.assumption: Noisy outlier features will not vote consistently for any single model, whereas sufficient inlier features agree on a good model.
assumptions.breaks_when: Outliers exhibit structured patterns or collinearity that vote consistently for a spurious model, or the inlier proportion is insufficient.

assumptions.assumption: A problem-specific error threshold $t$ exists that adequately separates inliers from outliers.
assumptions.breaks_when: The noise scale is unknown, non-uniform, or improperly tuned.

failure_modes.signature: All generated model hypotheses tend to be ranked equally good.
failure_modes.cause: The error threshold $t$ is set too large, causing outliers to be admitted into the consensus set.

failure_modes.signature: Estimated model parameters fluctuate unstably upon the addition or removal of a single datum.
failure_modes.cause: The error threshold $t$ is set too small, excluding valid noisy inliers from the consensus set.

failure_modes.signature: Candidate model is rejected because the consensus set contains $d$ or fewer points.
failure_modes.cause: The initial sample subset contained outliers or the dataset has a low inlier ratio (e.g., below 50%), yielding too few points within threshold $t$.

failure_modes.signature: The algorithm fails to recover either model instance correctly.
failure_modes.cause: Multiple valid model instances exist in the data, whereas RANSAC constructs a single consensus set for one model.
